boolean_surfaces.name: Boolean Surfaces: CSG as Composition
boolean_surfaces.v1_4_note: Reactivated as a spine sequence (order 12.7). Constructive Solid Geometry — union, intersection, difference of primitives — as the algebra of composed solid form. Sits between isosurfaces and softbodies.
boolean_surfaces.truth: Composition is not addition. Boolean ops give us a lawful way to compose solids: A∪B, A∩B, A−B. Every architectural cavity is a difference; every joint is an intersection.
boolean_surfaces.qfep_connection: Boolean operations are the smallest non-trivial calculus on solids. Pure F: deterministic composition without entropy term. Architectural cavity = difference; joint = intersection.
content: Boolean_Verbs: A ∪ B, A ∩ B, A − B on one pair of operands — only the word changes
Boolean_Gallery: six families at every value their DNA axis can take; the published claim beside the object
Boolean_Works: CSG at architectural scale — the workbench, the cavity, the cavern, and the interior the physics never arrives for

deferred_reason.Chamber_Boolean: chambers removed from the spine (Palle, 2026-09-02): the catalyst chambers leave the walk; the map stays on disk

artifact_groups.rationale: The three operators on one pair of operands, in three bays separated by sills rather than walls, so each verb stays visible from the next. the_argument_of_solids closes the hall by rebuilding all three at bench scale.

Six promoted families, each placed at all four values of its DNA axis — 24 placements in six bands. Layout is generated from the registry, default leftmost, so every band opens on the object as it ships elsewhere.

CSG at the scale where it would have to be architecture. The hall's finding is negative and deliberate: twelve of the chapter's thirteen artifacts carry no collision construct, so every large negative here is a picture of an interior rather than one.
